chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abi Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who loses consciousness during the day, then regains it before sunset. He said: 'He prays Dhuhr and Asr. And at night, if he regains consciousness before Fajr (dawn), he makes up the night prayer.'

This report confirms what we have previously stated: that it is obligatory upon him to make up the prayer during which he regains consciousness. And this time is the final time for the one compelled (by illness/unconsciousness), so at that moment it becomes obligatory upon him to make it up.

key_terms.اَلْمُضْطَرِّ: the compelled / one with valid excuse (for delayed prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up prayers if one regains consciousness before sunset or dawn?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ruling for *al-mudtir* (the compelled one) who regains consciousness before sunset, mandating the performance of Dhuhr and Asr along with the night prayer (*Salat al-Layl*) if conscious before dawn. It serves as a critical confirmation that the moment of regaining consciousness sets the definitive deadline for making up the missed prayer, distinguishing it from cases where consciousness is lost until after sunset. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the immediate obligation of *Qada'* once the state of compulsion ends within the prayer's time window.
